scenes.headline: How libfx keeps an agent turn alive through a crash
scenes.sub: The engine under Vercel's open-source HTML artifact builder
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Quoit! Vercel open-sourced an app that writes one web page per prompt. The agent loop underneath is the interesting part.

scenes.text: libfx stores every prompt before accepting it and every step as the turn runs, so a new process continues a killed turn instead of starting over.
scenes.mark: continues a killed turn instead of starting over
scenes.say: Every prompt and every step is stored first, so a new process continues a killed turn instead of starting over.

scenes.title: One turn, written down as it runs

steps.say: Your message lands in the session log before the server accepts it.
One worker holds the session. A replaced worker is refused at its next write.
It calls the model, runs the tools, and writes each step back to the log.
If the process dies, a new one replays the log and carries on.

scenes.title: A tool call cut off by the crash
scenes.say: The hard case is a tool that was running when the process died.

items.say: An idempotent tool runs again, under the same execution id.
Any other tool never runs twice on its own.
The model is told it may have partly run, and decides whether to check.

left.title: Rerun the turn
left.say: Rerunning the turn pays for every model call again, and might refund twice.

right.title: Continue from the log
items: Each tool says if it may rerun
right.say: The log replays finished calls, and each tool says whether it may rerun.

steps.say: In fx0, the chat, Redis and Neon belong to the app.
The libfx agent saves every step to Workflow World, and Vercel Queues restarts a crashed turn.

scenes.title: Model requests per turn, killed mid-turn
scenes.note: fake local model, SIGKILL, then resume
scenes.say: On a fake local model, a kill inside a tool still meant three model requests. A kill mid request re-sent only that one.

scenes.label: worst wait after a crashed prompt request on Vercel
scenes.note: 800 s limit plus a 5 s backstop
scenes.say: On Vercel, a crashed function looks like a slow one, so recovery can wait for the eight hundred second limit.

scenes.text: A crash-safe agent comes down to one question per tool: can this run twice?
scenes.say: One question for every tool. Can this run twice?

recap: Store the prompt and every step
Replay finished steps, never re-send them
Rerun only tools that say they may
scenes.say: Store every step. Replay what finished. Rerun only what says it may.
